source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Clutch and Transmissions, p.7-6

procedures.title: Three-speed transmissions (Saginaw and Warner): general description
notes: Saginaw 3-speed: all forward gears synchronized, helical gears throughout. Main drive gear rides on a ball bearing at the front of the case and pilots in an oil-impregnated bushing in the crankshaft. Mainshaft front pilots in rollers inside the hollow main drive gear; its rear rides on a ball bearing at the front of the extension housing.

Saginaw countergear runs on one row of rollers at each end, with thrust washers between the gear ends and the case bosses. An anti-rattle plate at the front of the countergear spring-loads the counter and clutch gears to damp torsional vibration. Reverse idler turns on an in-place bored bushing on a short shaft, held forward by a snap ring.

Borg-Warner heavy duty 3-speed: same layout but built for high torque and speed, with heavy duty ball bearings, double-row countergear rollers, and a reverse idler on 25 roller bearings with thrust washers.
Shifting: rods to the rear side cover lever for first/reverse, and a cross shaft to the front side cover lever for second/third.
Each synchronizer is a clutch hub, clutch sleeve, two key springs and three energizer keys, held on the mainshaft by a snap ring.
All forward gears are synchronized, so sequential downshifts for engine braking need no double-clutching. Reverse is not synchronized but is a helical gear for quiet running.
The manual does not say here which car lines use the Saginaw or the Warner unit.
